summary:
I built the HMDA buyer profiles by census tract, county subdivision (CCD), place (CDP) and ZIP (ZCTA) for all islands, with 2025 as the main year and a CCD-level comparison with 2019. Loan counts match the existing `an/new/hmda.json` county totals in both years, and a separate recomputation in pandas matched every CCD and every tract with 20 or more loans.

**Output:** `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-moku/72fb7234-fad9-5bdc-aaaa-c922016ddc21/scratchpad/an/gap/hmda_tract.json` (includes source, method, checks, notes and key figures).
- Scripts are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-moku/72fb7234-fad9-5bdc-aaaa-c922016ddc21/scratchpad/pull/gap_hmda_tract/`.
- Raw Census downloads and `MANIFEST.txt` are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-moku/72fb7234-fad9-5bdc-aaaa-c922016ddc21/scratchpad/raw/gap_hmda_tract/`.

**How it was done**
- **Loans included:** the same filters as `hmda.json` (originated, home purchase, site-built, 1–4 units). That gives 9,875 loans in 2025 and 13,797 in 2019, all lien positions kept.
- **Tract to CCD:** Hawaii's Census block files have no CCD column, so I took each census block's CCD from the TIGER/Line "faces" files and weighted blocks by housing units. Each tract goes to the CCD holding most of its housing units.
- **How clean the mapping is:** tracts sit inside a single CCD almost everywhere. Two tracts on Maui are split; their 25 loans in 2025 went to the larger side (Kahului and Kihei).
- **2019 comparison:** HMDA uses 2010 tracts for 2019 and 2020 tracts for 2025, so I built a mapping for each. CCD codes are the same in both years, so CCD comparisons are like-for-like. Tract-level results can't be compared across years.
- **Place names:** a tract gets a CDP name if that CDP holds at least 60% of its housing units. Otherwise it is labelled "mixed tract" or "outside a single CDP". ZIP groups use the same idea (50% threshold).
- **Small cells:** every group with fewer than 20 loans is flagged, and the rankings below use only groups with 20 or more.

**Key figures (2025)**
1. **Coverage:** 9,875 loans across 394 tracts. The 153 tracts with at least 20 loans hold 7,278 loans (73.7%).
2. **Kauai, second-home + investor share** (loans coded second home or investment, divided by all loans in the area): Koloa-Poipu CCD 72.3% (n=83) and Hanalei CCD 71.2% (n=80). At tract level, the Poipu tract is 86% (n=50) and Princeville 78% (n=59).
3. **Maui, same share:** Lahaina CCD 68.0% (n=122), up from 47.8% (n=435) in 2019. Kihei CCD is 48.7% (n=228). The Kaanapali tract (315.03) is 82% (n=45).
4. **Hawaii Island, same share:**
   - Pahoa-Kalapana CCD 52.4% (n=82), almost all of it investment loans (47.6%).
   - North Kona CCD 41.1% (n=409) and South Kohala CCD 40.6% (n=217).
   - The Waikoloa Beach Resort / Waikoloa Village tract (217.08) is 65% (n=107).
5. **Oahu, same share:** 15.7% island-wide. The Waikiki ZIP 96815 is 54.5% (n=378), and Waikiki tract 19.01 is 90% (n=30). Koolauloa CCD is the highest Oahu CCD at 31.9%.
6. **Highest median applicant income by island** (median over loans that report income; thousands of dollars, not adjusted for inflation):
   - Kauai: Hanalei CCD $406k.
   - Maui: Kula CCD $325k; the Wailea tract inside Kula CCD is $509.5k.
   - Hawaii Island: North Kona CCD $222.5k.
   - Oahu: Koolaupoko CCD $230k; the Ko Olina tract is $534k (n=26).
7. **VA-heavy areas on Oahu** (VA loans divided by all loans):
   - 27.1% island-wide.
   - By CCD: Ewa 44.1% (n=2,618), Waianae 37.1%, Wahiawa 36.4%, Koolaupoko 32.8%, Honolulu 10.4%.
   - Ocean Pointe CDP is 70.9% (n=158). 19 Oahu tracts are at least half VA; the highest is tract 84.07 at 81% (n=42).
8. **Median property value by CCD** (HMDA reports values as $10k bands, so these are band midpoints): highest are Kula $1.66M and Hanalei $1.39M; lowest are Pahoa-Kalapana and Kau at $335k and Keaau-Mountain View at $420k.
9. **Lahaina after the 2023 fire:** purchase loans in Lahaina CCD fell from 435 in 2019 to 122 in 2025 (−72%). Median income rose from $154k to $298k. Tracts mainly in Lahaina town had only 21 loans in 2025.

**Caveats**
- HMDA has no cash purchases, so these shares describe financed buyers only.
- Lenders changed how they split second homes from investment loans between 2019 and 2025, so compare the combined share rather than either part.
- Income is missing for 645 loans in 2025, many of them investor loans, so income medians in investor-heavy areas cover only part of the buyers.
- Molokai (27 loans) and Lanai (5) are reported at island level only. Every CCD there, plus Hana and three on Hawaii Island, has fewer than 20 loans and is flagged.

problems: Minor, wording: the Maui income key figure cites the Wailea tract 303.07 ($509.5k) and says nothing about the highest-income Maui tract, Kaanapali 315.03 at $547k (n=45, 40 report income). The Oahu figure, by contrast, cites its top tract (Ko Olina $534k). The numbers are right but the framing is inconsistent and could be read as Wailea being the Maui maximum.

Minor, summary prose: the caveat lists the CCDs under 20 loans as Molokai, Lanai, Hana and three on Hawaii Island. It leaves out Kaumakani-Hanapepe CCD on Kauai (n=11). The JSON itself flags it (low_n_flag=true, and it appears in highlights Kauai.groups_with_n_lt_20), so only the summary text is incomplete.

Cosmetic: low_n_fields leaves out median_property_value_first_lien and median_loan_amount_first_lien in 9 groups for 2025 and 6 for 2019, even though those medians rest on fewer than 20 values. All of these groups already have low_n_flag=true, so no small cell goes unflagged.

Edge case, not disclosed: in 2019, one loan is geocoded to the offshore water tract 15009990200, which has 0 housing units. It is assigned to Kula CCD because Kula has the most blocks there, and it shows up as a place group 'Kula CCD, outside a single CDP' (n=1, flagged). The notes only say water tracts have no 2025 loans. This does not materially affect the results.

Disclosed, worth keeping in mind: split tract 15009032000 (Maalaea–Launiupoko; 44% of its housing units are in Lahaina CCD) is counted in Kihei CCD in both years (11 loans in 2025, 24 in 2019). Lahaina CCD totals therefore leave out the Launiupoko side, but the treatment is the same in both years, so the -72% comparison holds.
Rounding: Haiku-Pauwela's median of 1,255,000 is shown as $1.25M while Hanalei's 1,385,000 is shown as $1.39M, so half-way values are rounded inconsistently (probably a float artifact). Trivial.

Labelling: 'Kailua CDP' appears under Koolaupoko CCD (Oahu, n=244) and under North Kona CCD (Hawaii Island, Kailua-Kona, n=235). These are different CDPs, so any downstream use needs to keep the CCD or island name attached.

summary:
I pulled district-level buyer origin for all 26 Title Guaranty districts across the four islands, for full-year 2025 and Jan–Jun 2026. I added 2024 and Jan–Jun 2025 for comparison. In every period, the district totals add up exactly to the island totals TG prints.

**Output:** `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-moku/72fb7234-fad9-5bdc-aaaa-c922016ddc21/scratchpad/an/gap/tg_districts.json`. It contains source, method, notes, checks, a one-row-per-district summary, the full tables, year-over-year changes, revisions between editions, and a list of TG's own inconsistencies.

**How the numbers were built**
- The table at the foot of each district page gives a "US TOTAL" and a "FOREIGN TOTAL" per district, but doesn't say which column is which district. I matched each column to its district panel by the fill colour drawn in the PDF. A second colour check agreed for every panel. The numbers also match the earlier `an/new/tg.json` exactly (130 records, 0 differences), which used a different matching method.
- Per district:
  - total sales = US TOTAL + FOREIGN TOTAL
  - Hawaii-resident buyers = the "HI" row
  - other-US buyers = US TOTAL minus Hawaii buyers (TG's US TOTAL includes Hawaii residents)
  - foreign buyers = FOREIGN TOTAL
- My shares match TG's printed percentages within 0.5 points. The Hawaii-buyer sums match each island's printed Hawaii count.
- **Names:** I used TG's printed district names. Most of the names in your request don't exist in the PDFs:
  - **Oahu:** Honolulu, East Honolulu, Leeward, Central, Windward, North Shore
  - **Maui County:** Central, South Side, Up Country, West Side, North Shore, East Maui, Molokai, Lanai
  - **Hawaii Island:** Puna, Kona, Kohala Coast, Hilo, Kau, North Kohala, Hamakua (there is no Waimea district)
  - **Kauai:** Lihue, Koloa, Kawaihau, Hanalei, Waimea
- **Dollars:** TG doesn't print a total dollar figure for each district. It prints Hawaii-buyer dollars plus the top 4 other states and top 3 countries. I kept those as partial "listed" figures, with how much of the category they cover.
- **Small numbers:** every row lists which counts are below 20. East Maui and Lanai have fewer than 20 sales in total in most periods. Foreign counts outside Honolulu are almost all below 20.

**Key figures**
1. **Honolulu district (2025):** 5,135 sales, 320 foreign (6.2%). That is 90% of Oahu's 356 foreign buyers. In Jan–Jun 2026 it had 181 foreign of 2,186 (8.3%), 93% of Oahu's 195.
2. **Highest Hawaii-resident share, Central Oahu:** 94.1% in 2025 (1,630 of 1,733) and 94.7% in Jan–Jun 2026.
3. **Hanalei (Kauai) is the most out-of-state district:** 66.2% other-US in 2025 (90 of 136) and 70.4% in Jan–Jun 2026 (38 of 54). Hawaii buyers spent $104.6M there; the California buyers listed spent $183.5M.
4. **Kohala Coast (Hawaii Island), 2025:** 47.0% other-US (302 of 643). The 132 California buyers spent $555.2M (about $4.2M each), against $386.4M from 328 Hawaii buyers. Kona was 43.3% other-US (331 of 764).
5. **Maui West Side:** 46.7% other-US in 2025 (84 of 180), up 14.0 points from 2024 (32.7%). Jan–Jun 2026 was 41.1% (37 of 90). South Side was 36.6% other-US with 7 foreign buyers out of 309.
6. **Hawaii Island districts were redrawn between editions.** The Q4 2024 edition shows 2024 Kohala Coast at 1,364 sales and Kona at 90. The Q4 2025 edition restates 2024 as Kohala Coast 699 and Kona 754. Together they are unchanged (1,454 vs 1,453), so about 665 sales moved from Kohala Coast to Kona. The new split is already used in the Q2 2025 edition, and TG gives no explanation. I couldn't check the Q1 2025 edition because its link redirects to TG's home page. For trends, use the restated 2024 figures; the 2023 and original 2024 figures are on the old split.
7. **Other 2024 restatements:**
   - Maui: Up Country went from 243 to 260 (other-US 37 to 52), South Side from 444 to 435, and Central from 374 to 365.
   - Oahu: districts changed by -4 to +5.
   - Jan–Jun 2025 as reprinted in the Q2 2026 edition differs only for Maui Central (172 to 170) and South Side (147 to 149).
8. **Oddities kept as published:**
   - Hilo's 2024 other-US count of 279 includes 232 California buyers ($35.0M, about $151K each), against 88 other-US in 2025. That inflates Hilo's 2024 other-US share (41.8%) and Hawaii Island's.
   - Kauai's Lihue fell from 170 sales in Jan–Jun 2025 to 66 in Jan–Jun 2026 (-61%).
9. **TG error on Kauai:** in 4 of the 5 Kauai editions, the countries printed in the Koloa and Lihue panels don't match those districts' foreign totals. They look swapped between the two. I used the foreign totals, which agree with TG's own pie-chart percentages. Only 0–2 sales per period are affected.

Scripts are in `scratchpad/pull/gap_tg_districts/` (`districts.py`, `build.py`, `finalize.py`). The manifest is `scratchpad/raw/gap_tg_districts/MANIFEST.txt`. It records the failed Q1 2025 download and confirms the 20 input PDFs still match the earlier download (same checksums).

checked.claim: Matching method: I wrote my own parser (vparse.py) in pull/gap_tg_districts-verify/. It does not use fill colours. It builds words from de-duplicated characters, then matches each foot-row column to a district panel by finding the assignment that best fits the printed pie % (HI / other-US / foreign) and the rule HI <= US TOTAL in both periods.
checked.recomputed: All 20 PDFs gave one clear best assignment. The total pie error was 3.1 to 5.3 points; the next-best assignment was at least 4.9 points worse (in most files about 1,000, because it broke the HI <= US rule).
checked.note: Every computed pie share was within 0.5 points of the printed value. Every island-share % I could read (16 editions) was within 0.5 points. In the Q4 2024 editions my parser did not read the island-share %. One panel name per Q4 2024 edition (Hamakua, Hanalei, Maui North Shore) was filled in by elimination, and I confirmed each against the page text.

summary:
I found no public owner-mailing-address data for Hawaii County or Kauai County. Nothing I could reach without getting past a bot check or login has owner mailing city, state, ZIP or country. Because of that, the Oahu-style breakdown can't be computed for either county: Hawaii vs mainland vs foreign, top states, mainland metros by ZIP3, foreign countries, district/ZIP, condo vs not, and addresses shared by 10+ parcels. The output file lists every place I searched and what to ask each county for. It also adds three partial public figures, with validation and caveats.

**Where I searched**
- **County ArcGIS Online:** I checked the field list of every public layer and table. Hawaii County has 222 services (272 layers/tables); Kauai has 616 services (911 layers/tables). They carry owner names only (Hawaii County: major-owner fields; Kauai: first owner).
- **Hawaii County's own GIS server (gis.hawaiicounty.gov):** the RPT, Planning_TaxMapping and Planning folders need a login ("Token Required").
- **Property tax websites:** hawaiipropertytax.com and the qPublic record pages are behind a Cloudflare bot challenge. kauai.gov returns an Akamai 403 and kauaipropertytax.com resets the connection. I didn't try to get past any of these.
- **Wider ArcGIS Online:** 109 keyword searches; I checked 1,359 services from the results. Copies of parcel data with mailing fields exist only for Maui and Oahu.
- **State of Hawaii Statewide GIS Program:** neither its map server nor its parcel download files have mailing fields (Hawaii County file 135,718 records; Kauai 25,119). Its metadata marks the county owner field "NOT TO BE DISTRIBUTED TO PUBLIC". The state and county open-data catalogs had nothing more.

**What to request:** the file names who to ask in each county Finance Department and exactly what to ask for. The main ask is mailing state, ZIP5 and country by parcel (including condo unit). A cheaper alternative is counts by tax district and mailing state, or for Hawaii County, access to the login-gated RPT map services.

**Partial figures:**

| # | Figure | How computed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hawaii County: 10.2% of homes owned out of state (2,367 of 23,277), about 2023 | Regrid's public census-tract layer (an outside data vendor), counts only. It covers just 35 tracts, so it does not represent the island. |
| 2 | Hawaii County coverage is uneven: Puna 771 homes vs 23,139 built-on parcels (3%); Ka'u and North Hilo have no data | Tract centers matched to the State's tax-district map, compared against built-on parcel counts from the county's 2026 roll |
| 3 | Hawaii County by district: North Kona 15.4% out of state (6,382 homes), South Kohala 14.8% (3,503), South Kona 13.1% (1,270), South Hilo 4.5% (10,797) | Out-of-state homes ÷ homes per district |
| 4 | Checked against our full Oahu and Maui rolls: Oahu 7.2% vs 7.4% from the roll (other US states only; districts differ by 0.7 pts on average). Maui 24.4% vs 27.8% (districts differ by 7.0 pts) | Regrid figures compared with owners_oahu and owners_neighbor. Regrid matches mainland-owned shares but seems to leave out foreign owners and drop condo units, so the Kona and Kohala resort figures are likely too low. |
| 5 | Kauai: Regrid has no Kauai tracts at all | Counted tracts for Kauai's county code (15007) |
| 6 | Kauai vacation rentals, 2021: 40.1% flagged Kauai-owned, 4.3% other-Hawaii-owned, 55.6% neither (1,029 records) | County layer, counted on the server. How the flags were set isn't documented, and the layer covers only part of the 3,974 vacation-rental-class records in the 2026 tax data. |
| 7 | Kauai vacation rentals with no local flag, by district: Koloa 61.0% (328), Hanalei 60.3% (481), Kawaihau 32.2% (143). Lihue has only 20 records, so its cells are marked n<20. | Same layer, by tax district |
| 8 | Kauai LLC-owned parcels, 2025: 2,584 (838 of them condo units). That is about 9.5% of non-owner-occupied residential (935), 6.8% of vacation rental (270) and 0.7% of owner-occupied (83) | County Housing Agency layer counted by tax class; class totals come from the 2026 tax data, so shares are approximate. This is ownership type, not mailing location. |

Every count cell carries an n<20 flag. The output has no owner names, street addresses or parcel IDs. The Kauai counts were computed on the county's server without downloading any owner records.

problems: Six small cells are unflagged, so the claim that every count cell carries an n<20 flag is overstated. In the Regrid tables flag_n_lt_20 tests only the homes count. Out-of-state counts under 20 are therefore unflagged: North Kohala zone has 7 (based on 171 homes), and five tract rows have 4, 10, 17, 19 and 7 (one of them a 22-home tract). The Kauai tables do flag cells like these, so the two parts of the output are inconsistent.

The Maui district check compares different things. Its roll side is owners_neighbor maui by_tmk_zone, which counts all parcels (80,457). The Oahu side uses residential class 1, and the Maui county-level check uses residential classes (64,795 parcels, 27.8%). The output does not say this. The 7.0-pt average also includes zone 1, which has only 11 homes and is flagged n<20; without it the average is 6.0 pts.

'838 of them condo units' (Kauai LLC) is misleading. A live TAXCLASS × TYPE count shows 484 of the 838 CPR units are Agricultural class (likely ag-land CPRs). Only 226 are non-owner-occupied residential, 57 vacation rental and 23 owner-occupied.

The Regrid caveat on the percent fields understates the main pattern. It cites peroutzip = 1 - peroutst, which holds in only 13 of 372 tracts. In 346 tracts peroutzip = outzip/homes, consistent with the field alias 'Out of Zip Code, In State'. The puller's (outzip - outstate) reading is still supported: 11 tracts have outstate + outzip > homes, which the alias reading cannot explain. But the stated evidence (outzip >= outstate everywhere) is weaker than this, and the in-state outside-ZIP shares (Hawaii County 13.5%, vs 23.7% under the alias reading) depend on that reading.

'Checked 1,359 services' slightly overstates the wider search. That is the number of unique service URLs requested; only 1,256 returned a readable schema. Of the 103 that never did, most are malformed layer-level geodata.hawaii.gov URLs (covered by the separate State scan) and 30 are token-gated, including a Hawaii Island 'KonaBaliKaiParcels' service. This does not change the not-found conclusion.
Minor manifest issue: peek/p24_count.json appears twice. The first row's sha256 and byte count refer to content that was later overwritten. The 9 ERR rows correctly have no file.
Minor format point: the output has no top-level 'method' key. Methods are recorded per source under source.partial_sources.*.method and method_per_publisher.
